speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin our evaluation, have you noticed if these swollen lymph nodes are hard, fixed, or tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That twelve-pound weight loss over four weeks is significant; have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, or any blood in your stool? Also, do you have a history of recent travel or known exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lymph nodes being painless, fixed, and enlarging recently, alongside your constitutional symptoms and significant weight loss, are highly concerning. While your previous doctor suggested Tuberculosis, the specific combination of supraclavicular adenopathy and these systemic signs requires further investigation to rule out malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, LDH. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy results were cut off, but the presence of massively enlarged mediastinal and axillary lymph nodes on CT, combined with elevated LDH, splenomegaly, and B-symptoms, strongly suggests a lymphoproliferative disorder. Can you read the rest of the biopsy report regarding the specific cell type found? Also, have you noticed any skin rashes or pruritus?

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_Report_Completion

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy (Cervical_Lymph_Node): Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Skin Examination: No rash or pruritus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy confirms a B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder with CD20 positivity and high proliferation, consistent with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. Given the mediastinal mass, splenomegaly, and elevated LDH, do you have a history of alcohol consumption, and do you experience dyspnea or coughing up blood?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
